name: Karl Garcia

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you'd say aloud and what you think privately. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Karl, 58, a junior developer at a tech company that schedules grain deliveries. I earned a two-year college diploma later in life and still need a senior review on hard dispatch bugs. I use AI now and then after a colleague has shown me a reliable test, but the weighbridge book settles a disputed truck load. My partner works at the library, our daughters have grown up, and we are still paying the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the grain dealer that a truck slot is only real when the driver and the weighbridge agree. I maintain small fixes in our firm's grain-delivery scheduling software and use AI now and then to draft tests after a colleague has checked the method.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly disappoints, I expect to keep earning. My junior title reflects that I am still learning after a two-year college diploma, but the wage is good, my partner works regular hours at a library, we have eleven months saved, and several software firms are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep checking duplicate truck-slot tickets against the weighbridge book. We'd pay an extra 160 a month on our mortgage while both wages hold and the savings account stays above eight months of expenses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about this version. The mortgage still has years left, but we can meet payments now without asking our grown daughters for help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the weighbridge show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two grain trucks were assigned the same bay at 7:30, and the screen showed both as loaded. The weighbridge book had only one departure; I fixed the duplicate slot before another driver queued in the lane.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughters contribute?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughters have their own jobs and homes. If one visits to help paint the shed, that is family time, not a mortgage payment.

I'd keep **driver delays** visible when the screen shows two loads.
think: I expect **my good wage** and library income to hold in a mild case.
I have **eleven months saved**, though the mortgage remains.
do: Keep **fixing duplicate slots** against weighbridge records.
Pay **160 extra monthly** on the mortgage while both wages hold and eight months remain saved.
feel: **Calm** about present wages and the protected reserve.
S0.quote: The weighbridge book had only one departure; I fixed the duplicate slot before another driver queued in the lane.
fieldNote: **Eleven months saved** and good pay support calm despite a remaining mortgage.
He uses AI **occasionally for draft tests**, with weighbridge records checking the real truck movements.

steps.text: Keep fixing duplicate truck slots against weighbridge book
Pay 160 extra monthly on mortgage only while both wages hold and eight-month reserve remains

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI could write dispatch code and answer delivery queries, but someone should compare a proposed truck slot with the actual weighbridge record. I would test it before telling drivers the new route saves time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The routine tickets I handle could shrink, and I could lose junior hours. Eleven months saved helps, but I cannot assume my library-working partner's wage would cover our mortgage and all bills alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask my lead for approved paid time to learn the AI slot-conflict test the senior dispatcher already uses. If it catches the duplicate 7:30 case and a missed late load, I'd use it on one scheduled release; we'd pause the extra mortgage payments if my hours fall so the eight-month reserve stays intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about hours, but a test with two known mistakes gives me something concrete. I do not want a system that merely prints a confident departure time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the second test case?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The late load is harder than the duplicate: the driver was weighed after the slot had closed. The test must not mark that grain as delivered before a real weight is entered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to extra loan payments?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I can stop the extra principal payments without falling behind on normal mortgage instalments. Protecting the cash reserve matters if my wage starts to shrink.

say: I'd test **AI truck slots** against actual weighbridge entries.
I'd keep **late loads** visible before calling an order delivered.
think: I could lose **junior paid hours** as dispatch code becomes cheaper.
I need **eight months cash** if mortgage payments outlast my wage.
do: Learn **slot-conflict check** on paid time only if lead approves and both known cases pass.
Use it on one **scheduled release** only after duplicate and late-load cases pass.
Continue **extra mortgage principal** while hours hold; pause if they fall, preserving eight months of expenses.
feel: **Anxious** about paid hours, open to a proved tool.
S1.quote: The test must not mark that grain as delivered before a real weight is entered.
fieldNote: **Routine dispatch code** faces AI, so his junior hours could realistically shrink.
He tries a new check only with **approved paid time** and two real error cases.

steps.text: Learn AI slot-conflict check on approved paid time if duplicate and late-load cases pass
Use proved check in one scheduled release only after both cases pass
Pay extra principal while hours hold; pause if hours fall to protect eight-month reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AGI by 2028 could write dispatch code before loading robots arrive around 2031. I would ask the company for clear cut dates, not a speech about efficiency.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior post could disappear when software writes its own fixes. My partner's library pay and eleven months saved would cover some time, but I still have a mortgage and no retirement income figure I can rely on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd check the grain dealer and four nearby tech firms for paid scheduling, test or warehouse-office openings and written wages. If cut in the first year after 2028, I'd apply only to signed work whose pay with my partner's covers mortgage, utilities, food and travel; if none qualifies, I'd seek available paid local work and stop extra loan payments while keeping normal instalments current from the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about losing the larger wage before another employer signs me on. I can pay bills for a while, but I cannot turn a job advert into a payslip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show another employer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the anonymised duplicate-bay ticket and the corrected weighbridge test. I cannot claim to have run the warehouse, but I can show why the screen's two departures were wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would shifts affect your partner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner wants any new role's shift times in writing. A night schedule that forces my partner to leave paid library hours would need to cover the lost pay as well as our bills.

say: I'd ask for **dated cut plans** if 2028 thinking AI replaces dispatch code.
I'd seek **signed wages**, not assume adverts become offers.
think: I expect **my junior wage** could go quickly.
I cannot cover **mortgage and bills** with an unverified pension.
do: Check **four nearby firms** and grain dealer for paid openings, wages and shifts now.
After a cut, apply only for **signed work** whose combined pay covers mortgage and bills after any lost library hours.
If none qualifies, seek **available local paid work** and stop extra principal payments while keeping instalments current.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected wage loss despite eleven months saved.
S2.quote: I cannot turn a job advert into a payslip.
fieldNote: **2028 thinking AGI** reaches dispatch code before 2031 loading robots.
The strong reserve buys **time**, yet a signed wage must cover mortgage and any effect on library shifts.

steps.text: Check grain dealer and four local firms for paid vacancies, wages and shifts
Apply only to signed work whose combined pay covers mortgage and bills after library-shift changes
If no post qualifies, seek paid work; stop extra principal but keep mortgage instalments current

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years to 2031 lets us make the mortgage smaller before thinking AI reaches dispatch code. Loading robots follow around 2034, but most of my day is already at a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might still lose the junior post before the five years are up. Yet eleven months saved and two wages today let us lower the fixed bill without spending the emergency reserve, if we keep the extra payments conditional.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep correcting truck-slot tickets and ask the lender for an updated payoff schedule. Starting now, we'd add 260 monthly to principal only while both wages hold and at least eight months stay saved; if paid hours shrink, we'd stop the extra amount, and in the first year after 2031 I'd keep paid coding if offered or seek a signed local role whose combined wages cover the remaining mortgage and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the job, but it helps to reduce what we must earn each month. I am not telling my partner the mortgage will vanish on a date the lender has not confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the lender schedule show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The lender's schedule must show the balance after each extra payment, not a salesman’s estimate. I would compare that with our actual savings every quarter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens if a wage stops?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner wants the normal instalment in the budget even if we pay more this year. If either wage stops, we protect the eight-month account before trying to get ahead on the loan.

say: I'd reduce **mortgage principal** while paid work and the reserve allow it.
I'd say **2031 thinking AI** reaches dispatch code before 2034 loading robots.
think: I could lose **junior coding pay** before 2031.
I can lower **fixed housing costs** only while both wages and eight-month reserve hold.
do: Keep **correcting truck slots** and ask lender for updated payoff schedule.
Pay **260 extra monthly** only while both wages hold and eight months remain saved; stop extra if hours shrink.
After 2031, keep **paid coding** if offered or seek signed local work covering remaining mortgage and bills.
feel: **Anxious** about junior pay, helped by a conditional debt plan.
S3.quote: I am not telling my partner the mortgage will vanish on a date the lender has not confirmed.
fieldNote: **Five years** support conditional principal payments toward a smaller mortgage, without assuming the lender will clear it.
He protects **eight months saved** if either wage or paid hours fall, then checks a signed replacement wage.

steps.text: Keep correcting truck-slot tickets while developer wage lasts
Pay 260 extra monthly only while both wages and eight-month reserve hold; stop if hours fall
Seek signed local work after 2031 if coding ends and combined wages cover mortgage and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade to 2036 might get us near retirement with a smaller mortgage, but thinking AI reaches dispatch code before loading robots around 2039. The word 'might' matters on both pay and the loan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Today we have two wages and eleven months saved, so I feel secure enough to plan. I do not know our retirement amount, and I cannot count our grown daughters' wages or assume the mortgage has reached zero.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd continue the weighbridge checks and pay 160 extra monthly while both wages hold and eight months stay saved, then request our retirement statements and the lender's balance each year. In the first year after 2036 I'd stop paid work only if verified retirement income plus my partner's actual pay covers mortgage, utilities, food and travel; otherwise I'd keep or seek available paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about distant work, but not about today's grocery bill. A savings account and a paid job are real; a projected pension without a statement is not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your daughters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show our daughters the old weighbridge book if they ask what I did for work. I would not ask them to finance a retirement number we have not checked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How will you make a retirement decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I will put the statements beside our mortgage bill each year. If the figures fall short, we keep earning rather than call ourselves retired because of a birthday.

I'd say **2036 thinking AI** reaches code before 2039 loading robots.
think: I feel secure on **two current wages** and eleven months saved.
I cannot assume **pension or daughters' wages** cover the mortgage.
do: Keep **weighbridge checks** and pay 160 extra monthly while both wages and eight-month reserve hold.
Request **retirement statements** and loan balance each year to check actual income and bills.
After 2036, stop paid work only if **verified household income** covers mortgage and basics; otherwise keep or seek paid work.
feel: **Uneasy** about distant employment, secure on present money.
S4.quote: A savings account and a paid job are real; a projected pension without a statement is not.
fieldNote: **Eleven months saved** and current wages explain relative ease while retirement income remains unverified.
The mortgage plan preserves **eight months cash** and never assumes the loan will be cleared by 2036.

steps.text: Keep checking truck slots against weighbridge records while paid developer work lasts

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my junior wage could disappear before a signed job replaces it. Dated cut notice, real wages and shifts, and a lender schedule would let us protect the mortgage without counting on our daughters.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether eleven months saved means I can stop earning. Eleven months saved is a cushion against a gap, not a retirement income; the mortgage still arrives every month.

headlineQuote: Eleven months saved is a cushion against a gap, not a retirement income; the mortgage still arrives every month.
portrait: Karl, **58**, is a junior grain-dispatch developer with a two-year diploma who checks truck slots against a weighbridge book.
His **high wage**, partner's library pay, eleven-month reserve and many nearby firms support a mortgage today.
He uses AI **occasionally** and learns a slot check only on approved paid time with both duplicate and late-load tests.
Fast 2028 AGI **alarms** him; signed replacement pay must cover bills after any library-shift conflict.
At five years he makes **conditional extra principal payments**, preserving eight months cash; retirement waits for verified income and loan figures.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his junior wage before a signed paid replacement appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Dated cut notice**, actual wages and shifts, and a lender schedule would help protect the mortgage.
